meta.purpose: Website knowledge, build rankings and builder calculation layer.
meta.scope: Externally developed and imported ISFL/DSFL rosters. DSFL budget 250; no purchased traits. ISFL maxed templates include all attributes and all purchasable portal traits; the build-WAR rankings use maxed ratings with only the traits whose fitted effect was positive.
meta.engine_policy: All current research (the native attribute matrix and the build-WAR study) uses the native C# port of the game engine (DDSPFHeadless.Native). The stock DDSPF21 engine is permanently retired for research; older studies that used it (the DSFL 40-game screening with finalist confirmation, and the ISFL attribute-cohort games) are kept as labeled history.
meta.source_path_base: Game workspace root. Cited decompiled files require the original decompilation; they are not included in the evidence ZIP.

DSFL.engine: Stock DDSPF21 engine (earlier study; superseded by the build-WAR rankings).
DSFL.display_selection: Highest mean treated-team score margin among tested profiles within archetype and role.
DSFL.finalist_selection: Role-wide top two distinct imported builds by screening margin, across all archetypes and profiles.
DSFL.confirmation: Fresh seeds in the same four matchups, both treated sides; finalist paired contrasts preserve A-minus-B orientation.
DSFL.interpretation: Absolute margins include host team/opponent strength. All 17 simultaneous 95% finalist intervals include zero.
DSFL.host_conditions: Late-season host skills and experience (0–3) retained; injuries disabled.

ISFL.interpretation: Maxed examples are legal cap-complete templates that buy every portal trait; those all-trait templates were not raced head to head. The build-WAR study measured maxed builds with the traits whose fitted effect was positive (see the build-WAR rankings). Analytical leaders compare the named attribute component only.

NATIVE_COHORT.engine: Native C# port of the game engine (DDSPFHeadless.Native); the stock DDSPF21 engine is retired for research.
NATIVE_COHORT.design: Same frozen 24 attribute/position experiments, six rating arms and adjacent higher-minus-lower contrasts as the existing accepted cohort study, on the same two fixtures; independently frozen job manifest and seeds, including a separate additional-replicates expansion.
NATIVE_COHORT.excluded_cohorts: Punter is empty on every touched team and side in both leagues, so kick-power-p and kick-accuracy-p have zero executable games on either engine. One ISFL matchup side also has zero rostered CB, losing that side for two more experiments. All exclusions come from roster composition alone, decided before any game ran.
NATIVE_COHORT.interpretation: Bonferroni-120 simultaneous 95% margin intervals exclude zero for 43 of 220 checked contrasts (110 per league) in the pooled base-plus-expansion dataset. The 24 mechanisms this matrix exercises were checked against the decompiled source before trusting these numbers (23 of 24 exact matches; the one confirmed gap was fixed, and fixing it required a second, previously-latent fix).
NATIVE_COHORT.confirmation_status: A same-seed comparison of the native port against 155,520 already-completed stock-engine games checked 16 of the 43 significant contrasts: all 16 were statistically consistent after multiple-comparison correction (3 showed nominal-only differences that did not survive correction). The other 27 contrasts were never checked against the stock engine and will not be: the stock engine is retired for research, so these are native-engine findings.

evidence.validation: Earlier stock-engine campaigns used one lookup-table initialization (34 penalties and 74 injuries); earlier duplicated-table campaign outputs are excluded.
evidence.export: Automatic TE traits are portal assumptions; private roster-export mapping remains unverified. Portal kicker unlock names increase caps, not stock named-trait effects.
evidence.optimality: The ISFL builder returns the exact optimum of the Builder win model (build_war.builder_model; anchored per position to direct paired measurements); its WAR is a model prediction. Its recommended builds were then played directly against the league-average starter and the fully maxed build on identical games (build_war.leagues.ISFL.builder_validation; earlier versions and their status in builder_validation_v1/_v2). The DSFL 250-TPE builds are measured directly; DSFL budgets below 250 project the earlier recipe and carry no game prediction.

notation.R: inclusive integer draw; min>=max returns min
notation.E: Endurance in endurance facts; Energy is current state

evidence_policy.reviewed_source_audit: Condensed reviewed use inventory; scope is not a complete executable function
evidence_policy.examples: Arithmetic or application examples, not additional empirical trials
evidence_policy.trait_absence: No direct named effect means none was identified in reviewed searchable source; it does not establish a hidden bonus or prove global inactivity.

Random-player injury gate is R(1,100)<8; targeted-player gate <10, with TeamID=0 excluded. They draw an injury severity and a second roll. Severity>70 succeeds when second roll>n; failing that, severity>30 succeeds when roll>n-5; severity<=30 when roll>n-35. **A severe injury draw can still succeed via the second branch**: E76 random-player n101 eliminates first comparison >101, but second comparison >96 still permits a severe injury. build_war.war_definition: Wins per regular season above a league-average starter at the same role (tie = half a win), from paired simulations: the build and the baseline play the identical matchups and random seeds, with the player locked to that role on the depth chart.

QB.label: Quarterback
QB.caveat: The starter under center or in the shotgun on every snap.

RB.label: Running back
RB.caveat: The lead back. The engine rotates backs by fatigue, so he plays about two thirds of the snaps.

FB.label: Fullback
FB.caveat: On the field in two-back sets, about 56% of snaps; mostly blocks.

WR1.label: Outside receiver (WR1)
WR1.caveat: Lines up outside on every snap. Return Specialist is tested here as a receiver, not as a returner.

TE1.label: Tight end (TE1)
TE1.caveat: On the field almost every snap; runs routes on about three quarters of passes and blocks on the rest.

C.label: Center
C.caveat: Snaps the ball and blocks the middle of the line.

LT.label: Left tackle
LT.caveat: Blocks the left edge of the line.

LG.label: Left guard
LG.caveat: Blocks between the left tackle and the center.

RG.label: Right guard
RG.caveat: Blocks between the center and the right tackle.

RT.label: Right tackle
RT.caveat: Blocks the right edge of the line.

LE.label: Left end
LE.caveat: Rushes the passer from the left of the three-man front.

RE.label: Right end
RE.caveat: Rushes the passer from the right of the three-man front.

DT1.label: Nose / defensive tackle
DT1.caveat: Rushes the passer from the middle of the three-man front.

MLB1.label: Middle linebacker
MLB1.caveat: Mostly drops into zones or covers a man; rarely sacks the quarterback.

LOLB.label: Left outside linebacker
LOLB.caveat: Blitzes off the edge, and with the right outside linebacker is the team's main source of sacks and tackles for loss.

ROLB.label: Right outside linebacker
ROLB.caveat: Blitzes off the edge with more man coverage than the left side, and is the team's leading tackler.

CB1.label: Outside corner (CB1)
CB1.caveat: Plays man coverage on almost every pass.

NB1.label: Nickel corner (NB1)
NB1.caveat: The fifth defensive back, on the field only in the 3-3-5 (about 65% of snaps).

SS.label: Strong safety
SS.caveat: Plays shorter zones and blitzes more than the free safety, with twice his sacks.

K.label: Kicker (also punts)
K.caveat: Also punts: these leagues roster no punter.

build_war.optimizer: Exact optimum of the fitted additive role model for one archetype at a TPE budget: every kicker cap-unlock prefix and every purchasable-trait subset (trait prerequisites become rating floors; unlock and trait fees are deducted; automatic traits are always included at no cost), then a knapsack over the 14 ratings using portal tier prices. Predicted WAR = season games x beta.(x(build) - x(baseline)) + anchor.offset_war, the role calibration to direct paired measurements; SE = sqrt(season games^2 x d cov d + anchor.offset_se^2); 95% interval = +/- 1.96 SE. The anchor is constant within a role, so the optimal build is unchanged. Mirrors build_war_model.optimize() with spend_eps = builder_optimizer.spend_eps: every rating option's knapsack value gets + spend_eps x its TPE cost, trait/unlock subsets are compared on value + spend_eps x total TPE spent, and the reported value/WAR excludes that tie-break.
build_war.builder_model: monotone: every rating tier's win value constrained >= 0 unless the unconstrained estimate is significantly negative (z <= -3.0); ISFL only

builder_optimizer.note: objective = model value + spend_eps x TPE spent (tie-break toward spending on tiers valued at exactly zero); reported value excludes the tie-break
